label_adjudication: FOREX_NG3_BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION is the correct plan-allowed terminal label; FOREX_NG3_REJECT_ALL would be wrong. Plan section 2 (frozen before any proposal) lists BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION among the five terminal outcomes; section 5 places the selection freeze (S) after D2 and before implementation — with all four proposals VETOed at D2 pre-score, the S freeze has zero eligible families, no frozen spec exists, no runner was built, no cell was scored, and the budget correctly stays 0/6 with the GO phrase REGISTERED_NOT_CONSUMED (its prelaunch gate never convened). REJECT_ALL is the label for a completed falsification in which cells RAN and lost: the ng1 precedent closed REJECT_ALL with 6/6 scored cells, 0 survivors, GO consumed, budget 6/6. Calling ng3 REJECT_ALL would fabricate a scored falsification that never executed. The cross-cycle precedent line is uniform: FOREX-NG2 BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION (0 cells, P0 floor fail), CRYPTO-V17 CLOSED V17_BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION (0 scored cells, budget 0/6 unconsumed), STOCKS-FREE-V12 TERMINAL_CONFIRMED_BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION. The D2 handoff's 'pointing the cycle toward FOREX_NG3_REJECT_ALL after the phase-gate review' is a lane recommendation ('advisory'), not a terminal registration; the plan's own taxonomy governs, and under that taxonomy selection-empty-pre-score is BLOCKED_DATA_OR_SELECTION. The label is also honest in the negative-first sense the plan declares ('a correct FOREX_NG3_REJECT_ALL is a successful research run'): the substantive result — CA-anchored revision dynamics produced zero ancestry-clean, identifiable, feasible families — is preserved in the D2 evidence and the ledger rows the controller appends at close.
